wins.label: Strong quarterly earnings
wins.evidence: the firm reported net income of $15 billion, EPS of $5.24 on revenue of $45.7 billion, with an ROTCE of 21%

wins.label: Markets revenue growth
wins.evidence: Markets revenue was up $1.1 billion or 15%. Fixed income was up 14%... Equities was up 15%

wins.label: Strong Investment Banking momentum
wins.evidence: IB fees were up 7% year-on-year. We continue to rank #1 with wallet share of 8.9%... Our pipeline remains robust, and the outlook along with the market tone and sentiment is notably more upbeat

wins.label: Raised NII guidance
wins.evidence: we now expect NII ex Markets to be approximately $92 billion, with the increase driven by changes in the forward curve and strong deposit growth

wins.label: Healthy consumer credit
wins.evidence: the consumer basically seems to be fine... Our delinquency rates are also in line with expectations. You saw that we kept our net charge-off guidance unchanged

risks.label: Deposit margin compression
risks.evidence: NII ex Markets was down $185 million, or 1%, driven by the impact of lower rates and deposit margin compression

risks.label: Increased expenses
risks.evidence: on adjusted expense, we now expect it to be about $95.5 billion, primarily driven by the impact of the weaker dollar

risks.label: Tariff uncertainty
risks.evidence: after the initial shock of the tariff policy changes, everyone kind of went on hold... there are a lot of risks

risks.label: Regulatory capital constraints
risks.evidence: G-SIFI inhibits... both a little bit of lending and a little bit of market making. LCR inhibits both because it's a very rigid way of looking at the bank balance sheet

risks.label: Peak private credit concerns
risks.evidence: I also think you may have seen peak private credit a little bit... credit spreads are very low. It's grown dramatically over time, and you have to pay up a lot for it
